newsitem.title: UK: Early ideas point to tighter 97-98 sugar mkt-Man.
newsitem.headline: Early ideas point to tighter 97-98 sugar mkt-Man.

text.p: Preliminary figures support the view of a potentially tighter 1997/98 world sugar market, according to trade house E D & F Man.
"Talk of a tighter season to come in 1997/98 has helped to support the market, despite the adequate supplies generated by the 1996/97 crops," Man said in its Sugar Situation report.
Man will be publishing its first estimates for the new season in September, it said.
"Much of this outlook depends on the premise that the world's largest producer, India, will have a significantly lower crop," it said.
Indian plantings are expected to be lower "due to widespread farmer dissatisfaction because of late payment for their cane."
EU crops are unlikely to repeat the higher yields of last season and the outlook for the leading east European crops is "not encouraging," Man said.
But good crop prospects across central America counterbalance this, Man said.

"Developments in Brazil will, as usual, be key to the market," it said. "Despite the planned increase in alcohol production, some of the projected higher cane availability is expected to be used for sugar," Man said.
